newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-UEFA TO CONDUCT PROBE INTO BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA TO CONDUCT PROBE INTO BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: UEFA, European soccer's governing body, decided on Tuesday to conduct its own probe into allegations of bribery and match-fixing after a meeting with the Portuguese Football Federation.

Gilberto Madahil, chairman of the PFF, met with UEFA officials, including beleaguered president Lennart Johansson, who is currently embroiled in his own controversy, and handed over documents related to charges that Porto sought to bribe a referee before a Euroepean Cup Winners' Cup semi-final match against Aberdeen 12 years ago.
"We are concerned with defending the integrity of European competitions," said UEFA general secretary Gerhard Aigner following the two hour meeting.
"They handed over documents and explained what they know so far.
"We are now going to hand over those parts that concern European competition to our own disciplinary body. They will look at them and decide how to proceed."
The information that was presented to UEFA was mostly reports that have appeared in the media.

They include a video cassette interview with businessman Fernando Barata who claims he was asked to approach the Romanian referee in charge of the Porto-Aberdeen game and offer him money to secure a 3-0 win for the Portuguese side in the home leg.
Porto won both legs 1-0. Both Porto and the match official have denied any bribery attempt was made.
The meeting was the second in as many days for Portuguese officials.
On Monday, Madahil met FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter, who indicated he was satisfied with the way the investigation was proceeding and noted it was an internal matter.
The PFF will continue to conduct its own investigation seperate from UEFA's but said it will co-operate fully with the European governing body.

"It started out as a purely domestic matter and the Portuguese football authorities are dealing with the it," said Aigner. "But when matters come up that concern European competitions it is also a matter for us."
UEFA said it would not be investigating any other allegations of wrong-doing within Portuguese soccer.
Porto are also at the centre of another controversy over the payment of a holiday in Brazil for referee Carlos Calheiros in the summer of 1995.
The club has officially admitted that it picked up the 700,000 escudo ($4,600) bill but says that it did so without realising who it was for.
